text: Age: 73
Occupation: Attorney

As a tenants' rights attorney and eight-year Santa Monica City Councilmember (including two years as Mayor), I have spent nearly twenty years fighting to keep Santa Monica renters securely and affordably in their homes.

At Western Center on Law & Poverty, I represent tenants facing displacement. On the City Council and Planning Commission, I championed lowering the cap on annual rent increases to 3% for rent controlled tenants, protecting Section 8 renters from discrimination, preventing rental units from being converted into short-term rentals like Airbnb, and shielding teachers and students from mid-year evictions. I was a proponent and funder of Measures GS-GSH (2016) and GS (2022), which together have generated more than $60 million to date for financial and legal assistance to at-risk Santa Monica renters, and for affordable housing creation.

I want to serve on the Rent Control Board to continue defending our renter neighbors against displacement, and our rent-controlled housing stock against redevelopment into luxury housing. I believe tenants should never be displaced from their homes absent a genuine safety necessity.
I do not accept, and will not accept, contributions from corporations, developers, or landlords.
I ask for your vote.

text: Age: 39
Occupation: Producer/Campaign Manager

Kurt Gonska currently serves as a Commissioner on the Santa Monica Rent Control Board. Elected in 2022, he served as Board Chair in 2025. Living in rent-controlled apartments in Santa Monica since 2014, Gonska is a strong supporter of rent control and has fought to protect and strengthen it because it enables tens of thousands of middle class and low income people to contribute to the vitality of Santa Monica. Rent control stabilizes our community and provides cost predictability to the people who call Santa Monica home.

During his four years on the Board, Gonska was instrumental to increasing standards for how much tenants can receive in rent decreases for loss of amenities or deteriorating conditions, banning algorithmic price fixing software, developing Charter amendments that are on the ballot this November, and hiring a new Rent Control Executive Director and General Counsel.
Gonska's professional experience includes producing live events, marketing, and political campaign management.

Kurt Gonska stands on the shoulders of the activists who delivered rent control to Santa Monica in 1979 and fought to protect it for decades. He will continue fighting to fix the housing affordability crisis so that everyone in our community can thrive.

text: As a renter in the Pico Neighborhood, I understand the experiences and challenges faced by

Santa Monicans who rely on rent control to stay in their homes. I have been a community advocate working behind-the-scenes for many years to fight against evictions and displacement. Through my lived experience with my family, I've earned the trust necessary to connect tenants, the agency, and the Board in order to provide the information and assistance residents need. It is crucial that tenants and landlords are aware of their rights and responsibilities.
My goal is to help our community exercise its rights as tenants.
If elected, I will enforce our rent control law and support any amendments or legislation that benefit renters. As a Commissioner, I will advocate

for our community by working alongside stakeholders to ensure that our rent control laws remain strong and effective. I will be a fair and impartial decision-maker who can work effectively with both tenants and owners.

I know how important it is for our city to protect families from being priced-out of Santa Monica. We are stronger as a community when we know that our representatives support and take care of our interests.

text: I'm Heather Thomason, a Sunset Park mother, a writer, and a proud union member of the Writers Guild of America. I'm running for the Rent Control Board because I've lived the difference rent control makes. For 16 years I was a renter. I watched my rent jump 50 percent in a single year, then lost the next place I moved into when the landlord sold the unit. Displaced too many times, I sought out rent-controlled housing; its stability allowed me to start my own family and save toward a home of our own. I've now started answering calls on the Santa Monicans for Renters Rights tenants rights hotline and helping neighbors facing displacement. On the Board, I'll work to protect our rent-controlled housing from demolition and from state laws that put it at risk. I'll also help our most vulnerable residents stay in our city for the long term through stronger enforcement against harassment, education around typical buyout amounts, and helping connect renters who face eviction to assistance before they lose their homes.

text: Age: 57
Occupation: Small Business Owner

It is vitally important that the Santa Monica Rent Control Board remains renter-centered. This is why I am running for the Santa Monica Rent Control Board to ensure policy decisions represent the best interests of residents.

My priorities are to establish an Ethics Commission for greater staff transparency, accountability, and operations oversight; increase protections and resources for disabled and roommate renters; establish cohesion and integration of the Code Enforcement Department and the City Attorney Consumer Protection Division; and provide greater oversight of the Judicial Affairs of the Rent Control Administration. Santa Monica Rent Control needs proactive leadership that is responsive to the renters of the city and fights the increasing tenant harassment strategies property owners use to force renters out of their rent-controlled units. We need to host Legal Clinics in Santa Monica parks.

I am a 24-year renter/resident, small business owner, founder of Compassionate Santa Monica, Giving Tuesday Santa Monica, bilingual educator, community advocate, and former Santa Monica College student (member of the SMC General Advisory Board). I am committed to ensuring Santa Monica remains affordable and accessible to residents of every background and ability in every neighborhood of our beloved city.
I am proud to be endorsed by local leaders from our neighborhoods and neighboring cities. I am asking and would be honored to have your vote.
